title: Token wavefront throttle and deadline conservator for continuous batching
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem statement: continuous-batching admission controls and batch shaping today treat requests as independent slots and use static heuristics tuned for average throughput. This leads to P95/P99 tail spikes when a mix of long-prefill, CPU-bound attention requests, and short interactive decodes converge onto the same GPU pool. Goal: design and implement a lightweight, cross-tenant token-wavefront-based throttle coupled with a deadline conservator that reduces tail latency while preserving throughput and fairness.
acceptance_criteria: 1) P99 latency for mixed workload lab scenario reduced by >=30% vs baseline under 2x load; 2) End-to-end throughput (tokens/s) does not drop >8%; 3) No single-tenant starvation observed in fairness test; 4) Operable via runtime flags and exposed metrics in console; 5) Feature has canary rollout plan and automatic fallback.
design_notes:
Core idea: maintain a compact, per-worker token-wavefront estimator (TWE) that tracks outstanding token work per logical stream and a soft deadline conservator that assigns micro-deadlines to prefills/decodes. Admission decision = score(TWE, predicted-kernel-fit, tenant-priority) -> lease token windows with soft preemption. Key pieces:
- TWE uses EWMA over token service time and increments on admission, decrements on completion. Keeps fixed-size ring buffer per worker (O(1) memory).
- Kernel-fit advisory: lightweight model that maps sequence-length, attention-type, and quantization flags to expected kernel latency distribution; trained offline and shipped as a tiny lookup table.
- Deadline conservator: computes micro-deadline = now + latency-budget * urgency-factor; urgent short decodes get smaller factor. If conservator predicts miss, we either downgrade kernel variant or defer admission by a token-smoothing interval.
- Soft leasing: admission grants are leases that can be partially revoked with TTL; revocations prefer downgrade to fallback model variant before outright preemption.
Tradeoffs: extra bookkeeping per-worker increases CPU overhead slightly; kernel-fit table must be kept up to date for new model variants; leasing introduces complexity for correctness in streaming flows.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 wks): implement TWE skeleton and telemetry hooks; add per-request metadata for sequence-length and attention flags. Phase 2 (2 wks): integrate kernel-fit lookup and scoring; build admission scorer and simulated scheduler mode. Phase 3 (2 wks): implement soft-lease API and conservative revocation path; wire fallback model variants. Phase 4 (1 wk): e2e lab tests, perf runs, and console metrics. Phase 5 (1 wk): canary rollout.
test_plan: Unit tests for TWE accounting; simulator tests covering mixed workloads (interactive decodes, long prefill, bursty microbursts); integration with kernel-fit table using synthetic sequences; fairness regression tests with per-tenant weighted traffic. Performance harness: two cluster profiles (dev-small GPU pool, staging-simulated-1000qps) running 30-minute runs measuring P50/P95/P99 and throughput.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag default=off. 2) Canary at 5% traffic for dedicated dev pool for 24h, monitor P50/P95/P99 and throughput. 3) If no regressions, increase canary to 25% for 48h. 4) Full rollout gate with automatic fallback if P99 > baseline+15% for 10m. 5) Post-rollout observational window 72h.
monitoring_metrics: twe.active_leases (gauge), twe.predicted_tail_ms (histogram), admission.score_distribution (histogram), soft_lease.revocations (counter), kernel_fit.match_rate (ratio), p50/p95/p99_token_latency (histogram), per-tenant_starvation_alert (binary). Alerts: p99 regression, revocation surge, kernel_fit_mismatch_rate>5%.
tasks: Create TWE data structure and API in runtime (ENG change)
Add per-request metadata plumbing to front-end ingress
Implement kernel-fit lookup table and ship initial table for open-models
Write admission scorer and integrate with scheduler interface
Implement soft-lease and revocation paths with fallback handlers
Add telemetry and console dashboard charts
Create simulator scenarios and perf harness jobs
Prepare rollout feature flag and canary automation
risks: 1) Kernel-fit lookup inaccuracies for new model variants could cause misrouting; mitigation: conservative default that falls back to safe kernel. 2) Lease revocation may complicate streaming semantics for long-lived sessions; mitigation: prefer model downgrade and inform client via explicit short header. 3) CPU overhead on control plane if TWE bookkeeping scales poorly; mitigation: micro-benchmarks and throttle sampling rate.
metrics_target: P99 tail down >=30% in mixed workload lab; throughput loss <=8%; per-tenant starvation incidents=0 in fairness tests.
